statement: For the exact finite Gaussian model, sum_k k a_k=n and Q_n(t)=sum_k k a_k exp(-(k-1)t).
proof_or_counterexample: Unique maximizer a.s.; weak gradient is path indicator with norm squared n; Hermite Parseval and Mehler diagonalization yield both sums. Detailed rederivation in w494/ATTEMPT.md.

statement: For D_n(K)=sum_{k<=K}k a_k, Var(M_n)<=D_n(K)+n/(K+1) and D_n(K)<=K Var(M_n); a polynomial bound on D_n at polynomial K would imply a variance power gain.
proof_or_counterexample: Termwise split of nonnegative chaos coefficients; the tail is at most total gradient energy n divided by K+1.
remaining_gap: G1, the polynomial D_n input, is unproved.

proof_or_counterexample: Compare exp(-(k-1)t) termwise in low k<=K and high k>K parts of the nonnegative overlap series.

statement: A root with m disjoint Gaussian n-vertex corridors has nonroot vertex marginal 1/m yet variance bounded above and below by constants times n/log m when m=n; this blocks a graph-generic marginal-to-power inference.
proof_or_counterexample: Independently checked T=g0+sqrt(n-1)max_j G_j; quantile u with Phi(u)^m=1/2 and Mills ratio give variance lower c(n-1)/log(2m); indicator hypercontractivity gives upper 2(n-1)/log m.
remaining_gap: Different graph; not a C0120 counterexample; G1 for quadrant lattice open.

statement: In the exact Gaussian source model, Var(M_n)=H_n+Var(M_n(r)); for fixed beta, Var(log Z_n)=beta^2 H_n+Var(log Z_n(r)).
proof_or_counterexample: Each layer mean is Gaussian-orthogonal and therefore independent of all centered residuals; its sum adds to every path energy and has variance H_n.
remaining_gap: Variance lower floor does not supply power upper bound.

proof_or_counterexample: Root overlap is one; endpoint signs of correlated Gaussian differences agree with probability 1/2+arcsin(rho)/pi; integral of arcsin(rho) over rho in [0,1] is pi/2-1.
remaining_gap: Finite-n witness only; no asymptotic upper bound.

statement: A polynomial-time bound Q_n(n^-a)<=C n^(1-b) implies Var(M_n)<=n^(1-a)+C n^(1-b), and a variance power delta implies a polynomial-time Q bound with exponent delta/2.
proof_or_counterexample: Split Var=integral e^-t Q(t)dt at tau=n^-a using Q<=n and monotonicity; converse uses (1-e^-tau)Q(tau)<=Var and 1-e^-tau>=tau/2.

statement: For the source model, D_n(1)=sum_v P(v in P_n)^2=lim_{t->infinity} E|P_n(g) intersect P_n(g^t)|>=H_n.
assumptions: iid standard Gaussian sites in nonnegative quadrant
proof_or_counterexample: Gaussian IBP gives first-chaos coefficient E[g_v M_n]=E partial_v M_n=P(v in P_n). Parseval yields D_n(1)=sum p_v^2. Each layer has i+1 sites and sum p_v=1, so Cauchy-Schwarz yields H_n. Mehler limit picks degree one.
